desc:
A pattern p consists of lowercase letters and two special characters: ? matches exactly one arbitrary character and * matches any sequence of characters, including the empty one.

A way to match is a cut of the whole string s into consecutive pieces, one piece per character of p in order, such that a letter takes exactly one character equal to it, a ? takes exactly one character, and a * takes any number (possibly zero) of characters. Two ways are different if some pattern character receives a different piece. Return the number of ways, modulo 1,000,000,007.

s = "abc", p = "*?*"  ->  3   (the ? can take a, b or c)
s = "ab",  p = "**"   ->  3   (the pieces are ("","ab"), ("a","b"), ("ab",""))
s = "aa",  p = "a*"   ->  1
s = "ab",  p = "a?b"  ->  0
s = "",    p = "***"  ->  1
constraints: s contains only lowercase letters; p contains lowercase letters, ? and *
hints: The yes/no wildcard matching problem uses a table over prefixes of the string and the pattern. What would you store in each cell to count instead of decide?
Let W[i][j] be the number of ways the first j pattern characters can consume exactly the first i characters of s. A letter or ? consumes one character, so it only looks at W[i-1][j-1] (if it fits).
For *, the star takes k ≥ 0 characters, so W[i][j] is the sum of W[i-k][j-1] over all k. That sum telescopes: W[i][j] = W[i][j-1] + W[i-1][j]. Take everything modulo 109+7.
editorial: Count paths instead of testing reachability. W[i][j] is the number of ways in which the first j pattern characters match exactly the first i characters of s. The base row is W[0][j] = 1 while every pattern character so far is * (each takes the empty piece) and 0 after the first non-star. The base column is W[i][0] = 0 for i > 0.

A letter or ? takes one character: W[i][j] = W[i-1][j-1] if it matches s[i-1], else 0. A star takes k characters for any k from 0 to i, so W[i][j] = sum_k W[i-k][j-1]; subtracting the same formula for i-1 shows that this equals W[i][j-1] + W[i-1][j], so each cell is O(1). The values are reduced modulo 109+7 because the number of ways grows quickly (many stars give binomial-sized counts). A rolling row keeps the memory linear.
